findings: The video adds analysis that no published source carries. It uses a fixed panel of 92 economies to cancel GitHub's own coverage growth (TypeScript economies reported rose from 93 to 162). It splits the answer into relative (18% to 49%) and absolute (gap 1.1M to 2.5M) halves, counts economies at or above 50% (47 of 92, up from 0), and compares year-on-year ratio gains. None of this is a restatement of an Innovation Graph page or of Octoverse.

Search (1 call, 'TypeScript JavaScript GitHub Innovation Graph Octoverse TypeScript overtakes'): the comparable content is GitHub's Octoverse 2025 (github.blog, Oct 2025), which says TypeScript became #1 by monthly contributors in August 2025, and its press echoes (InfoWorld, Visual Studio Magazine, InfoQ 2026-03, 36kr, heise 2024, vibe-data.com). None uses the Innovation Graph languages.csv, a fixed economy panel, a relative-vs-absolute split or a per-economy count. Nothing found says what this video says. (Grade: search snippets, not fetched pages.)

The narration is written for this question, not boilerplate. analyses/t1.json is a {fig:} template, but its qualitative words are specific to TypeScript and JavaScript ('Relative to JavaScript, yes, and quickly', 'because both languages grew', 'which is why we followed a fixed set'). Each word is guarded by a claim check in figures.json (ratio_rose, gap_widened, both_grew, last_year_fastest, picture_same: all hold). Measured independently: the ratio rose in 92 of 92 economies and the last-year gain was positive in 92 of 92, so 'the picture is the same' is not filler.

All six visuals are drawn by code from the pinned CSV for this analysis: pushers lines, ratio line, top-10 growth bars, year-on-year gain bars, per-economy histogram and coverage lines. Each carries the source and licence. There is no stock footage, no generative imagery, no third-party chart and no music.

Reused-content rule (youtube-monetization-policies.txt:144, :200, :204): not triggered. The underlying numbers are GitHub's CC0 data, but nothing is copied from another online source; the aggregates and charts are new computations. The limits paragraph paraphrases the datasheet's method, which is attribution, not a reading of someone else's material.

It falls outside the :138 example because that example requires 'minimal or no narrative, commentary, or educational value', and this video has a question, a two-sided answer, per-economy breadth and stated limits. It does add 'the creator's original, authentic insights' (:140) in the panel method and the relative/absolute split.
